title: Match Alphanumerical Pattern in Matrix I
summary: Given a 2D integer matrix board and a 2D character matrix pattern, find a submatrix of board that matches pattern.
statement: Given a 2D integer matrix board and a 2D character matrix pattern, find a submatrix of board that matches pattern. Matching requires that the dimensions of the matrices are identical, and for each letter in pattern, the corresponding cells in the submatrix must either match the digit or be distinct. Return the coordinates of the upper-left corner of the matching submatrix with the lowest row and column indices, or [-1, -1] if no match is found.
constraints: board is a nonempty rectangular digit matrix and pattern is a nonempty rectangular array of digit-or-lowercase-character strings that fits inside it.
Pattern digits must equal board digits literally; repeated letters map consistently to one digit.
Different letters must map to different digits; return the first matching top-left coordinate in row-major order, or [-1,-1].
hints: Letters form a bijection with the board values used by letters, while digit symbols are literal constraints.
Test placements in row-major order with forward and reverse maps local to each placement.
For every pattern cell, compare digits directly; for letters reject either mapping conflict, otherwise record both directions.
The two maps are exactly the consistency and distinctness rules, and the first successful row-major placement has the requested smallest coordinates.
editorial: The two maps are exactly the consistency and distinctness rules, and the first successful row-major placement has the requested smallest coordinates.

tests.explanation: At [0,0], a maps to one and b maps to two consistently, so the first submatrix matches.
No row has a second cell equal to literal digit one while maintaining the placement, so no match exists.
